'''''Sematophyllum''''' is the [[Type (biology)|type]] genus of the family [[Sematophyllaceae]].<ref name="Tropicos - Family">{{cite web |title=Sematophyllaceae Broth. |url=https://tropicos.org/name/35002815 |website=Tropicos |publisher=Missouri Botanical Garden |access-date=1 November 2025}}</ref>  It contains about 170 species.<ref name="Bryonames">{{cite web |title=A Synopsis of Sematophyllum |url=https://www.bryonames.org/nomenclator?group=sematophyllum |website=The Bryophyte Nomenclator |access-date=1 November 2025}}</ref>  ''Sematophyllum'' was described by [[William Mitten]] in 1864.<ref name="Description">{{cite journal |last1=Mitten |first1=William |title=Contributions to the Cryptogamic Flora of the Atlantic Islands |journal=The Journal of the Linnean Society, Botany |date=1865 |volume=8 |pages=3–10 |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/226560 |access-date=1 November 2025}}</ref>

''[[Sematophyllum demissum]]'' was designated as the type species by [[Max Fleischer (painter)|Max Fleischer]] in 1923.<ref name="Fleischer 1923">{{cite book |last1=Fleischer |first1=Max |title=Die Musci der Flora von Buitenzorg: zugleich Laubmoosflora von Java |date=1923 |publisher=Brill |location=Leiden |page=1261 |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/592376#page/1/mode/1up |access-date=10 January 2026 |language=German |format=PDF |trans-title=The Moss of the Flora of Buitsenzorg: also Deciduous Moss Flora of Java}}</ref>

==Etymology==
The name is derived from 'semato', meaning "marked" and 'phyllon', meaning "leaf".  The name refers to the enlarged alar cells that are characteristic of the genus.<ref name="Tropicos">{{cite web |title=Sematophyllum Mitt. |url=https://tropicos.org/name/35001196 |website=Tropicos |publisher=Missouri Botanical Garden |access-date=1 November 2025}}</ref>

==Morphology==
''Sematophyllum'' is often found in dense mats with creeping branches that are sparsely to freely-but-irregularly branched and densely foliate.  Branch cross-section exhibits small, thick-walled cells surrounding larger thinner-walled cells with no central strand.  Leaves are monomorphic between the stem and branch: arranged erect-spreading to homomallous to falcate-secund, lanceolate to ovate, acute to acuminate (rarely obtuse); margins are entire to serrulate distally and subentire proximally; costa absent or short and double.  Laminal cells are rhomboidal to linear, smooth or rarely unipapillose, often becoming shorter in the apical region.  Alar cells are enlarged and inflated, usually colored.  [[Seta#Plant_setae|Setae]] are smooth and usually reddish.  Capsules are ovoid to short-cylindric with collenchymatous exothecial cells.  [[Peristome]] is double, with triangular exostome teeth.<ref name="Buck 1998">{{cite journal |last1=Buck |first1=William R. |title=Pleurocarpous Mosses of the West Indies |journal=Memoirs of the New York Botanic Garden |date=1998 |volume=82 |pages=367–368 |publisher=The New York Botanical Garden |issn=0071-5794}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Sematophyllum Mitt. |url=https://www.worldfloraonline.org/taxon/wfo-4000035017 |website=World Flora Online |access-date=9 January 2026}}</ref>

==Range==
''Sematophyllum'' has a [[Cosmopolitan distribution|cosmopolitan]] distribution, having been found on every continent except Antarctica.<ref>{{cite web |title=Sematophyllum Mitt. |url=https://www.gbif.org/species/2680613 |website=GBIF |publisher=Global Biodiversity Information Facility |access-date=9 January 2026}}</ref>

==Position within the family==
Sematophyllaceae is a [[Monophyly|monophyletic]] family within [[Hypnales]] with two [[Phylogenetics|phylogenetically]] supported subfamilies, Wijkioideae and Sematophylloideae.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Hedenäs |first1=Lars |last2=Buck |first2=William R. |title=A Phylogenetic Analysis of the Sematophyllaceae |journal=Lindbergia |date=1999 |volume=24 |issue=3 |pages=103–132 |jstor=20150016 |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/20150016 |access-date=9 January 2026}}</ref>  ''Sematophyllum'' has been described as the "dregs" of Sematophyllaceae, being "characterized by the lack of various specialized features."<ref name="Buck 1998" />  Many genera within Sematophyllaceae are paraphyletic, including ''Sematophyllum,'' and it is the subject of ongoing scholarship.<ref name="Phylogeny 2017">{{cite journal |last1=Carvalho-Silva |first1=Micheline |last2=Stech |first2=Michael |last3=Soares-Silva |first3=Lucia Helena |last4=Buck |first4=William R. |last5=Wickett |first5=Norman J. |last6=Liu |first6=Yang |last7=Câmara |first7=Paulo E.A.S. |title=A molecular phylogeny of the Sematophyllaceae s.l. (Hypnales) based on plastid, mitochondrial and nuclear markers, and its taxonomic implications |journal=Taxon |date=August 2017 |volume=66 |issue=4 |pages=811–831 |doi=10.12705/664.2 |jstor=26824567 |bibcode=2017Taxon..66..811C |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/26824567 |access-date=9 January 2026}}</ref>
